direct_claims: This chart shows estimated annual global deaths from protein-energy malnutrition, broken down by age group.
The subject belongs to global health and mortality measurement.
The chart is presented by Our World in Data and cites IHME Global Burden of Disease (2025) as the data source.
The subtitle states that protein-energy malnutrition results from insufficient caloric and protein intake.
The chart indicates that estimates come with wide uncertainties, especially for countries with poor vital registration.
In public health terms, protein-energy malnutrition refers to severe undernutrition caused by inadequate energy and protein intake.
The uncertainty note is important for decision-making because weak death-registration systems can hide the true scale of malnutrition mortality.
The chart covers the world rather than a single country or region.
The time series runs from about 1980 to 2023.
Comparisons over time or across places may be affected by differences in diagnostic practices and death certification, according to the note.
derived_claims: Total deaths appear to decline substantially from the early 1980s to 2023, despite notable temporary surges. — derived by reading the overall stacked total trend across years.

Around the most recent years, the 70+ age group appears to account for a larger share than earlier in the series. — derived by comparing relative contribution of the 70+ band in early vs late years.

The increasing relative prominence of older age groups in later years may indicate that child malnutrition mortality fell faster than mortality at older ages. — derived by comparing age-band shares over time.

Children under 5 appear to bear the greatest burden in most years, which implies that food security, infant feeding, sanitation, and primary care systems are especially important for child survival. — derived from the dominance of the under-5 band in most years, with implication added from domain reasoning.
